transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you lately and what brings you here today?

I... well, I came in because I've been doing some things lately that are... out of character for me. Things that actually kind of scare me. Like, I'll just walk out in the middle of major software deployments at work, or I'll find myself driving around late at night with no real plan or destination. I don't know. It's just... that is not how I've ever handled stress before.
Have you ever felt like you're seeing or hearing things that others don't, or had beliefs that others say aren't true?
No. I haven't... I haven't experienced anything like that. Just the driving and walking out. Nothing else.
Have you ever experienced periods where you felt unusually energized, needed less sleep, or felt like your thoughts were racing more than usual?
No... I don't think so. I definitely haven't felt unusually energized or anything like that. Just... no.
Have you ever had times when you felt so good or so hyper that people around you noticed a change in your behavior or thought you were acting unusually?
No. I... I'm not really a hyper person. Nobody has ever pointed out anything like that to me.
Have you ever experienced any memory gaps, or times when you felt detached from yourself or as if you were watching yourself from outside your body?
No... I remember things fine. I haven't ever felt like I was outside my body or anything. Just... no, I haven't had that.
Have you ever felt like you're not all 'you,' or like there are different parts of you that act or think differently, almost as if there are multiple people inside you?
No. I'm just... me. I don't feel like there are other people in my head.
Have you experienced any particularly stressful or traumatic events recently before these behaviors started?
Yeah... I suppose. There was a... a late-night cutover incident. For work. Um... this has all been going on since then. It was a little over a year ago... about 13 months now, I guess.
Have you ever felt like you didn't know who you were, or like you were completely disconnected from your sense of self, even briefly?
No... I don't think so. I know who I am. I haven't felt anything like that.
Have you ever felt like you were losing your sense of who you are, or like you were watching yourself act as if you were a different person, even for a short moment?
No... I mean, I just said I know who I am. I don't... I don't feel like I'm watching myself or acting like someone else. It's just me.
Have you ever suddenly traveled to a new place and later been unable to remember why you went there or how you got there?
No. I haven't done that. I always know where I'm going.
Have you ever suddenly left your home or workplace and traveled somewhere without any clear reason, and later felt confused about who you are or couldn't remember your past?
No. I've never done anything like that. I don't... I don't just leave for no reason. I remember my past fine.

Can you describe exactly what goes through your mind just before you decide to walk out during a software deployment or start driving at night? Do you feel like you're making a choice, or does it feel more automatic, like you're not fully in control of the decision?

I... I don't really know how to describe it. I'm not sure exactly what I'm thinking in those moments. I just... I came in because I've started doing these things that scare me. Like walking out in the middle of a deployment, or just getting in my car and driving around late at night with no plan. 

I don't know if it feels automatic or if it's a choice. I just know it's... it's not how I've ever handled stress before.
During these times when you walk out or start driving, do you ever feel detached from your surroundings, like things seem unreal or distant, or as if you're in a dream-like state?
No, I don't think so. It doesn't feel like a dream. It's just... I just go. Everything looks normal, I guess.
When you walk out during a deployment or start driving at night, do you feel like you can't stop yourself, like you're not able to resist the urge to do it?
I don't know if I'd say I can't stop myself. It's not like that. I just... I just do it. I don't really think about stopping.
Before you walk out or start driving, do you feel like something inside you is pushing you to do it, even if you don't want to?
I... no, not really. It doesn't feel like I'm being forced or pushed to do it. I just... I decide to leave, and I do. That's really all there is to it.

When you walk out during a deployment or start driving at night, does it feel like you're acting on impulse without really thinking about it, or does it feel more like a deliberate decision you're making at the moment?
I guess it's... it's just a decision. I mean, I don't really think about it that much. I just decide I need to go, so I go.
Before you start driving at night or walk out during a deployment, do you feel a strong, uncomfortable urge or pressure that makes you feel like you have to do it, even if you don’t fully want to?
No... I don't feel any kind of pressure. Like I said, I just... I just go.

While you're walking out during a deployment or driving at night, do you feel fully aware and in control of what you're doing, or does it feel like you're on 'autopilot' without really thinking about it?

I... I know what I'm doing. I'm aware. It's just... I guess that's why I finally came in. I've started doing things that actually scare me a little. The walking out of deployments... driving around late at night with no real plan. I just... I've never handled stress this way before.

Before or during these episodes of walking out or driving, do you ever feel like you're not fully present, or like you're just going through the motions without really feeling connected to what you're doing?
No... not really. I'm there. I know I'm driving or walking. I'm not... checked out or anything.
